item.text: The web review produced recoverable, source-located material in all three selected themes. The strongest repairs are: an official NPT final-document section for 1B; the 2000 U.S. State Department report’s exact paragraphs on Al-Kush, emergency powers, Ibrahim, NGO prosecution, and government remedies for 3B; and a World Bank/IMF goal-to-implementation-to-outcome chain for 8B. I’m now separating these into atomic handoff units and marking prior composite or unsupported dispositions accordingly.

# Permissive research handoff — Mubarak / Egypt / 2000

Direct continuation completed for 1B, 3B, and 8B. No scores assigned.

## New source-claim units

### MUB-E059 — 2000 NPT Final Document: Middle East nuclear-free-zone commitments

- Claim: The 2000 NPT Review Conference reaffirmed the 1995 Middle East resolution, called for regional states to join the NPT and accept IAEA safeguards, and urged practical steps toward a verifiable Middle East WMD-free zone.
- Precise locator: Final Document, “The Middle East, particularly implementation of the 1995 Resolution,” paragraphs 1–10, especially paragraphs 3, 6, 7, and 9. The text is reproduced at the Arms Control Association’s transcription of the official document. [Arms Control Association](https://www.armscontrol.org/act/2000-06/2000-npt-review-conference-final-document#regional)
- Source summary: Official 2000 conference outcome; independent of the prior CNS analysis.
- Period fit: Exact 2000 conference outcome.
- Ruler attribution: Egyptian-state/diplomatic posture; the document does not establish Mubarak’s personal intervention. Retain as structural evidence unless separately supported by a named presidential act.
- Contrary evidence: The document records unresolved regional noncompliance and specifically identifies Israel’s non-accession; it is a negotiated multilateral text, not proof of implementation.
- Links: 1B.1, 1B.4, 1B.6, 1B.10.
- Disposition: `final_evidence` for Egyptian diplomatic posture; not direct personal attribution.

### MUB-E060 — Al-Kush investigation and state response

- Claim: The U.S. State Department reported that violence on January 2, 2000 killed 21 Christians and one Muslim; President Mubarak sent the Minister of Local Administration as his emissary, while the Minister of Housing and Public Prosecutor visited to investigate. The government provided compensation and rebuilt damaged kiosks.
- Precise locator: U.S. State Department Country Report 2000, sections 1(a)–1(c), paragraphs describing Al-Kush and government response, lines 395–397 of the Refworld transcription. [Refworld report](https://www.refworld.org/reference/annualreport/usdos/2001/en/25766)
- Source summary: Contemporary official human-rights report with event details, executive response, and remedial measures.
- Period fit: Exact January 2000 event and response.
- Ruler attribution: Direct for Mubarak’s dispatch of an emissary; structural for prosecutor, ministries, and police.
- Contrary evidence: The same report states the reopened police-brutality investigation continued without resolution and that most police-abuse cases did not receive adequate punishment (paragraphs 110–113).
- Links: 3B.1, 3B.2, 3B.4, 3B.7, 3B.9; 8B.9.
- Disposition: `final_evidence`.

### MUB-E061 — 2000 security-force abuse and incomplete accountability

- Claim: The 2000 State Department report says security forces continued arbitrary detention, mistreatment, torture, and mass arrests; local police also killed, tortured, or abused suspects and others. It reports that disciplinary action occurred in some cases but that most cases were not pursued or adequately punished.
- Precise locator: U.S. State Department Country Report 2000, paragraphs 110–112. [Refworld report](https://www.refworld.org/reference/annualreport/usdos/2001/en/25766)
- Source summary: Contemporary government assessment distinguishing counterterrorism abuses, ordinary police abuse, and weak accountability.
- Period fit: Calendar year 2000.
- Ruler attribution: Structural executive responsibility; the report identifies government and security-force conduct but does not prove Mubarak personally ordered each act.
- Contrary evidence: Some disciplinary prosecutions occurred; more than 1,300 political detainees were released (paragraph 113).
- Links: 3B.2, 3B.4, 3B.5, 3B.6, 3B.10.
- Disposition: `final_evidence`.

### MUB-E062 — Saad Eddin Ibrahim and EOHR: prosecution plus corrective outcomes

- Claim: The government arrested Ibrahim and closed the Ibn Khaldun Center on June 30, 2000; the State Department reports that observers viewed the prosecution as connected to remarks about senior officials and raised due-process concerns. Separately, charges against EOHR secretary-general Hafez Abu Se’da and attorney Mustafa Zidane were dropped in May 2000.
- Precise locator: State Department report paragraphs 220–227 and 349–352. [Ibrahim section](https://www.refworld.org/reference/annualreport/usdos/2001/en/25766) · [NGO/accountability section](https://www.refworld.org/reference/annualreport/usdos/2001/en/25766)
- Source summary: Contemporary official report covering both coercive prosecution and two documented case dismissals.
- Period fit: Exact 2000 arrests, trial opening, and charge dismissals.
- Ruler attribution: Direct government action; presidential direction is not established for each prosecutorial decision.
- Contrary evidence: Ibrahim was released on bail in August; EOHR charges were ultimately dropped; the government permitted a Cairo human-rights conference in October, while prohibiting another seminar in January.
- Links: 3B.5, 3B.8, 3B.9; 8B.2, 8B.8.
- Disposition: `final_evidence`.

### MUB-E063 — Higher-education reform goal and implementation chain

- Claim: A National Conference on Higher Education Reform met in February 2000. Its declaration, endorsed by President Mubarak, set a 17-year reform program covering university autonomy, funding reform, quality assurance, accreditation, faculty training, libraries, competitive funding, and technical-education reform.
- Precise locator: World Bank Report No. 24905-EGT, p. 16, paragraphs 27–28, lines 500–520. [World Bank PDF](https://documents1.worldbank.org/curated/en/246851468770078481/pdf/multi0page.pdf)
- Source summary: World Bank project/evaluation document describing the institutional process, presidential endorsement, intended reforms, and donor alignment.
- Period fit: Conference and endorsement exact to February 2000; implementation horizon explicitly long-term.
- Ruler attribution: Direct for presidential endorsement; implementation responsibility is shared with ministries, universities, and donors.
- Contrary evidence: The source describes a program and alignment process, but does not demonstrate completed 2000 outcomes; it expressly cautions that measuring some objectives remained premature.
- Links: 8B.1, 8B.2, 8B.3, 8B.6, 8B.7; secondary link 6B.2 and 6B.5.
- Disposition: `final_evidence`.

### MUB-E064 — Macro reform outcomes and policy constraints

- Claim: IMF reporting credits Egypt’s 1990s authorities with stabilization, liberalization, and privatization, but states that reform slowed in the late 1990s. Monetary tightening in 1999/00 stabilized reserves toward the end of 2000 while contributing to slower growth; revised fiscal accounting produced materially different deficit estimates.
- Precise locator: IMF 2001 Article IV notice, paragraphs under “Background,” lines 222–229. [IMF](https://www.imf.org/en/news/articles/2015/09/28/04/53/pn01116)
- Source summary: IMF assessment separating prior reform achievements, policy slowdown, 2000 stabilization effects, and measurement uncertainty.
- Period fit: 1999/00 and end-2000 outcomes, with some late-1990s context.
- Ruler attribution: Structural cabinet/economic-policy responsibility; no personal Mubarak decision is established for each measure.
- Contrary evidence: Reform progress slowed; growth fell from approximately 5% in 1999/00 to preliminary 3–3.5% for 2000/01; fiscal estimates varied substantially.
- Links: 8B.1, 8B.2, 8B.6, 8B.7, 8B.10; also 5B.3, 5B.4, 5B.6.
- Disposition: `final_evidence`.
